# Endor Labs EZ Scan — support skill

Support material for the `endor-ez-scan` agent. This skill documents the workflow, scan-type
matrix, reachability tags, and safety contract. The agent recipe
(`kiro-agent-kit/recipes/endor-ez-scan-agent.md`) is the behavioral source of truth.

## What it does

Two phases in one run:

- **Phase 2 (capability detection):** figure out which scan types apply to this repo and which
  the tenant is entitled to, before scanning. Never abort the whole run because one type is
  unlicensed or errors.
- **Phase 1 (broad scan):** one Endor MCP `scan` call covering every enabled type with
  `quick_scan: false` (full call graph → function-level reachability) and `summary: false`.

## Scan-type matrix

| Scan type | Endor MCP `scan_types` value | Gate |
|-----------|------------------------------|------|
| Dependencies (SCA) | `dependencies` | applies when manifests/lockfiles exist |
| Known vulns | `vulnerabilities` | baseline |
| Secrets | `secrets` | baseline |
| SAST | `sast` | applies when source languages detected; C/C++ opt-in via `languages: ["c"]` |
| AI SAST | `ai-sast` | tenant-entitled |
| GitHub Actions | `ghactions` | applies when `.github/workflows/` exists; tenant-entitled |

Separate lanes (not part of the single `scan` call):

- **Upgrade Impact Analysis (UIA):** read-only `endor-upgrade-impact` enrichment on top findings.
- **Container:** the `scan` tool takes no image target — recommend the container lane if a
  `Dockerfile`/compose/image is present.

## Reachability priority (from `quick_scan: false`)

| Priority | Dependency tag | Function tag |
|----------|----------------|--------------|
| P0 Fix now | REACHABLE_DEPENDENCY | REACHABLE_FUNCTION |
| P1 Investigate | REACHABLE_DEPENDENCY | POTENTIALLY_REACHABLE_FUNCTION |
| P2 Plan fix | REACHABLE_DEPENDENCY | UNREACHABLE_FUNCTION |
| P3 Track | UNREACHABLE_DEPENDENCY | UNREACHABLE_FUNCTION |
| P4 Ignore | PHANTOM | any |

## Preflight & safety

- Requires an authed `endorctl` + the Endor MCP `scan` tool. If unavailable, the agent returns
  `UNKNOWN` with `data_gaps` and points to `endor-agent-kit-setup`. It never runs
  `endorctl host-check`.
- Namespace is resolved from the user request, `ENDOR_NAMESPACE`, the default
  `~/.endorctl/config.yaml` namespace key, or resolved Project metadata — never dumped/echoed.
- Scan-enabled, otherwise read-only: **no** file edits (not even a result cache unless the user
  explicitly approves), package installs, git/gh mutations, PR/MR/comments, finding dismissals,
  or Endor policy writes.

## Host notes

- **Cursor / Kiro:** exposed as the `endor-ez-scan` agent (Cursor: `endor-ez-scan-agent`). The
  first `scan` call prompts for approval because scan tools are not in the MCP auto-approve list.
- **Kiro CLI vs IDE:** CLI gates via `toolsSettings.shell` (allow `endorctl scan`, deny other
  mutations); IDE gates via `permissions.rules` (`filesystem deny **`, shell allow incl. scan,
  deny other mutations). Both derive from the same recipe.
- **Claude Code:** exposed as the `endor-ez-scan` subagent; `Write`/`Edit` tools are disallowed
  so it can scan (Bash + MCP) but cannot modify files.
